mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the 3-month forward CPIAUCSL inflation forecast by the market leads to a preemptive rise in risk premia, depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL forecast crosses above 3.0% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during forecast-up periods (t-test p > 0.05); or CPIAUCSL does not cross the threshold in the forecast horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS coincides with stronger consumer confidence and higher wage growth, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the labor signal; or HOUST does not show a parallel upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed within one month by a rebound above the prior month's level signals a bottoming-out effect that boosts near-term equity valuations and drives positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO drops >10% in a month then recovers >5% in the following month
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward returns after such INDPRO pattern; or pattern fails to reappear in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS (raw materials orders) over three consecutive months, accompanied by a simultaneous uptick in GDPC1 (goods orders), predicts a supply-side soft landing that supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls >5% for 3 consecutive months while GDPC1 rises >3% over the same period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite the supply signal; or the interaction pattern is not statistically significant (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent tightening in the FEDFUNDS rate over two consecutive months produces a persistent discounting effect on long-term equity expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05); or FEDFUNDS does not exhibit two consecutive months of increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in UNRATE above 4% signals wage-price misalignment and impending labor market stress, which depresses risk appetite and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.0% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such UNRATE spikes (t-test p > 0.05); or UNRATE does not cross the threshold in the prediction window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in both PAYEMS (labor) and INDPRO (production) for two consecutive months indicates a dual softening in demand and supply, which amplifies uncertainty and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls >3% and INDPRO falls >8% in two consecutive months
regime_hint: dual softening in labor and production
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative during such dual contractions (t-test p > 0.05); or proxies do not move in the required pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to accommodative policy as reflected by a sustained monthly decline in FEDFUNDS below 4.5% for 4 consecutive months increases market expectations of future rate cuts, supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 4.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the accommodative window; or FEDFUNDS does not remain below 4.5% for the required duration in walk-forward tests.
